hero.emblem: Lumoxia emblem, an eight-point Sumerian rosette
hero.tagline: Ancient games, rebuilt as apps with new art and thoughtful software.
mission.lead: Lumoxia is an indie studio. The oldest games ever played are still good to play, and good art and software can bring them to new players.
mission.c1.p: Games that are thousands of years old, rebuilt with new art. The rules stay true to the original and the app is easy to pick up.
mission.c2.p: Simple rules, clear visuals and no ads.
mission.c3.p: AI tools are part of how Lumoxia is made, from design to code.
game.shot: {app:title} app showing a game in progress: ivory and carnelian stones on the board, the dice, and an Ivory to move message
game.p: One of the oldest known board games, played in Mesopotamia about 4,500 years ago. This version has new art and simple rules.
game.b1: Eleven board designs, including one based on the original board in the British Museum.
game.b2: Play a friend on one device, or play the computer.
game.b3: Nine languages. Works offline, with no account, no ads and no tracking. One optional, one-time purchase opens every board and stone colour.
music.p1: The game has its own soundtrack. Slow, warm and a little strange, it is written to sit under a long game of dice and stones rather than to compete with it. The tracks are made with AI tools, like the rest of Lumoxia, and shaped by hand until they sound right for the board.
music.p2: The soundtrack lives on Lumoxia’s Patreon page, which is also where you can help the work continue.
about.p: Giorgio is a computer scientist who has spent his career working on AI. He makes Lumoxia on his own, with AI companions and four cats, out of a long interest in ancient games.
contact.lead: It is not in the App Store or on Google Play yet. Follow the work on GitHub.

privacy.meta: {app:title} for iOS and Android. Last updated 25 October 2026.
privacy.short: In short: {app:title} does not collect any data about you. It has no accounts, no ads, no analytics and no tracking, and the game works offline. The only thing it sells is one optional unlock, paid for through the App Store or Google Play.
privacy.stores.h: What the app stores on your device
privacy.stores.p1: The app keeps a few things on your device only, so the game remembers them next time:
privacy.stores.l1: your settings: player names, stone colours, board design, language, sound and the shake-to-roll switch;
privacy.stores.l2: your game statistics: the results of games played on this device, shown in the Stats panel.
privacy.stores.p2: This information never leaves your device. Lumoxia cannot see it. You can erase the statistics at any time with “{app:statsReset}” in the Stats panel, and deleting the app removes everything.
privacy.not.h: What the app does not do
privacy.not.l1: The game itself sends nothing to the internet or to any server of ours.
privacy.not.l2: It does not use analytics, crash reporting, advertising or third-party software that collects data.
privacy.not.l3: It does not track you across other apps or websites and does not ask for tracking permission.
privacy.not.l4: It does not ask for your location, contacts, photos, camera, microphone or any account.
privacy.not.l5: It does not see or store your payment details. Apple or Google handles every payment.
privacy.iap.p1: The app offers one optional, one-time purchase that opens every board and every stone colour, now and in later versions. You can also unlock boards and colours for free by playing games. There is no subscription and there are no ads.
privacy.iap.p2: Apple or Google takes the payment and keeps the record of it, under their own privacy policies. Lumoxia receives no payment details and no personal information, and never learns who bought. To show that you own the unlock, the app asks the App Store or Google Play on your device, which may use the internet for that check. Nothing else is sent.
privacy.motion.p: If you switch on “shake to roll” (it is off by default), the app reads your device’s motion sensor while the game screen is showing, only to detect a shake. The readings are used on the spot and then discarded. They are never saved or sent anywhere.
privacy.links.h: Links that open in your browser
privacy.links.p: The Rules panel has links to other websites (for example the Lumoxia pages, a history video and the credits for the sound tools) and to these pages. When you tap one, your browser opens it. That website then deals with you under its own privacy policy, which Lumoxia does not control.
privacy.children.p: Because the app collects no personal information, it collects none from children either. Purchases are made through the App Store or Google Play, so their own parental controls decide whether a child can buy. Lumoxia does not control them.
privacy.site.p: If you choose a language, this site remembers your choice in your browser on your own device. It is never sent anywhere. The site sets no cookies.
privacy.changes.p: If the app ever changes what it does with data, this page will be updated and the date above before the change ships.
support.meta: {app:title} for iOS and Android. Last updated 25 October 2026.
support.intro: Need help with {app:title}, or found a problem? Write to the address below and you will get a reply.
support.subject: {app:title} support
support.include.l1: your device (for example iPhone 16, iPad Air or Pixel 9) and its iOS, iPadOS or Android version;
support.include.l2: the app version (shown in Settings → Apps → Royal Game of Ur);
support.include.l3: what you did, what you expected and what happened. A screenshot helps.
support.q1.a: Tap the book icon at the top left of the game for the rules. In short: roll the four dice, move one stone the number shown, land on a rosette for an extra turn, capture an opponent’s stone in the shared middle lane, and be first to bring all seven stones off the board.
support.q2.q: Can I play against the computer, or with a friend?
support.q2.a: Both. On the first screen choose “{app:modeShortHvc}” to play the computer or “{app:modeShortHvh}” to share one device.
support.q3.q: How do I change the language, sound or boards?
support.q3.a: The language button is at the top right. The gear icon opens sound settings, including the shake-to-roll switch. The board button on the first screen lists the eleven board designs.
support.q4.q: How do I reset or delete my statistics?
support.q4.a: Open {app:statsLabel} from the first screen. “{app:statsReset}” clears everything, and you can also delete a single player.
support.q5.q: Does the app need an account or internet connection?
support.q5.a: No account is needed. The game works offline and collects no data. The App Store or Google Play needs a connection only when you buy or restore the unlock. See the Privacy Policy.
support.q6.a: One optional, one-time purchase opens every board and every stone colour, now and in later versions. Boards and colours also unlock for free as you finish games, so the game is fully playable without paying.
support.q7.q: How do I restore my purchase?
support.q7.a: Open the purchase screen and tap “Restore purchases”, signed in to the Apple ID or Google account you bought with. This also works after reinstalling the app or on a new device.
support.q8.a: Refunds are handled by Apple for App Store purchases and by Google for Google Play purchases. Lumoxia cannot issue them. If something went wrong with the unlock itself, write to us and we will help.
